summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (May 2026) with hands-on firmware development across STM32 Cortex-M4, FreeRTOS, and Linux-based embedded systems. Experienced in bare-metal C, low-level peripheral drivers (I2C, SPI, UART, ADC), sensor integration, and hardware-firmware debugging aligned with BMC firmware and server hardware interfacing.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico and HC-05 Bluetooth; implemented sensor data acquisition and firmware stack for 3-DoF HID command translation.
Implemented a tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding with software calibration to eliminate sensor jitter across use cases.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member team across national-level competitions, owning PCB fabrication, embedded hardware integration, and firmware debugging end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed STM32 Cortex-M4 peripherals in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM firmware footprint at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver from scratch without HAL abstractions.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across sensor-reading and actuator-control tasks on STM32.
Implemented interrupt-driven UART communication between STM32 and Jetson host; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensor via I2C for real-time distance measurement.
Debugged hardware-firmware interactions between STM32 and peripheral devices using logic analyzers and oscilloscopes.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for contact-aware grasping; resolved 11 integration failures across sensor, servo, and system-level interactions.
Deployed full pipeline on NVIDIA Jetson running Linux; coordinated multi-layer debugging across hardware and embedded software layers.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
